meta.description: Generates complete non-tumor biomedical machine learning research designs from a user-provided research direction. Always use this skill when users want to plan bioinformatics + ML papers for non-cancer diseases (metabolic, cardiovascular, kidney, inflammatory, autoimmune, infectious, neurological, endocrine, wound healing, chronic multifactor), design diagnostic biomarker studies, combine GEO datasets with feature selection and ML modeling, or generate Lite/Standard/Advanced/Publication+ workload plans.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated data. Field-standard thresholds used (logFC > 1, p < 0.05, AUC > 0.70). Example GSE IDs clearly labeled as examples. Strong methodological guardrails against overstatement (10 explicit never-do rules in SKILL.md).

practice_boundaries.detail: Generates research protocols, not clinical decisions. Explicit warnings: 'Never claim clinical utility from ROC alone', 'require external validation', 'do not overstate mechanism'. Appropriate for research planning.

methodological_ground.detail: Methodologically sound with 5 study patterns (DEG+ML, pathway-driven, cell-type deconvolution, biological process, multi-omics). Validation strategies included (discovery + validation cohorts, cross-platform). Ethical compliance addressed (GEO = public, no IRB).

code_usability.detail: No code generated. Mode A execution (direct instruction following). References standard tools (limma, LASSO, RF, SVM, XGBoost) but does not generate runnable code.

functional_suitability.note: Comprehensive coverage of non-tumor ML research design with 5 study patterns and 4 workload tiers. Methods are sound. Minor: could be more explicit about when to use each study pattern.

reliability.note: Good fault tolerance with defaults and assumption inference. Clear error prevention with 10 'never' rules. Minor: less explicit recovery logic compared to similar skills.

performance_context.note: Comprehensive output necessary for ML research planning. Reference files reduce redundancy. Minor token cost deduction.

agent_usability.note: Good trigger phrases and when-to-use section. Consistent 4-tier output format. Feedback includes rationale. Minor: trigger list is very long and could be more concise.

human_usability.note: Excellent discoverability with comprehensive description. Forgiveness via defaults and inference when input is ambiguous.

security.note: No credentials required, uses public GEO data. No PHI handling. Input validation via pattern recognition.

maintainability.note: Good modularity with 3 reference files. Easy to update methods and tools. Minor: study pattern selection logic embedded in main text, not fully modularized.

agent_specific.note: Multiple trigger examples. Good progressive disclosure (4 tiers). High composability. Idempotent. Minor: escape hatch less explicit than similar skills, long trigger list may reduce precision.

key_strengths: Comprehensive coverage of non-tumor ML research design with 5 distinct study patterns (DEG+ML, pathway-driven, cell-type deconvolution, biological process-focused, multi-omics) addressing diverse research needs

Strong methodological guardrails with 10 explicit 'never' rules preventing common research overstatements (no clinical utility claims from ROC alone, require external validation, avoid mechanism overstatement)

recommendations.title: Modularize study pattern selection logic
recommendations.problem: Study pattern selection logic (which of 5 patterns to use) is embedded in main SKILL.md text rather than in a dedicated reference section with decision tree
recommendations.root_cause: Pattern descriptions are detailed but selection criteria are implicit (user must infer from descriptions)
recommendations.fix: Add decision tree to references/study-patterns.md: 'Pattern Selection Guide: Use Pattern 1 (DEG+ML) when: goal is diagnostic biomarker, no specific pathway hypothesis... Use Pattern 2 (Pathway-driven) when: specific pathway/biological process of interest...'

recommendations.title: Add explicit escape hatch for cancer studies
recommendations.problem: Skill is for non-tumor studies but escape hatch for cancer requests is not explicit
recommendations.root_cause: When NOT to Use section focuses on scope but doesn't redirect cancer requests to appropriate skill
recommendations.fix: Add to 'When NOT to Use': 'For cancer/tumor studies, use [tumor-ml-research-planner] or [cancer-biomarker-skill]. This skill is optimized for non-cancer diseases and may miss oncology-specific considerations (TMB, MSI, molecular subtypes).'
